checks.name: provider-invocation-graceful-stop-live-child
checks.summary: One real claude invocation per run, deliberately terminated while genuinely in flight so the control path of cap-loop-control could be proven to reach a real process. The child was located by scanning /proc for a direct child named claude, its process group was signalled, the supervised invocation returned, and the child's death was confirmed by bounded polling of /proc. Because the process is killed before it produces output, SupervisedInvocationRunner skips TrueUp by design, so each of these invocations stays in the ledger as state=reserved charged at the 1.00 USD worst case forever and carries no session_id and no usage counts. That is the intended fail-closed accounting, not a lost measurement. Sequences 4, 7, 10, 13, 16 and 19 are these invocations.
